name: T-Mobile Home Internet (5G Home Internet) and T-Mobile Fiber
notes: Researched from public t-mobile.com support pages and the public sign-in page only (no sign-in attempted). Home Internet is billed on the regular T-Mobile account (T-Life app / My T-Mobile) with a T-Mobile ID. Sign-in page observed: 'Email or phone number', Next (password on the next step), Sign up, and 'Pay as a guest' (no login), so loginSteps=2 and guest pay is supported. Home Internet customers get their One-Time PINs by email (mfa=email). Payments: no fee online or in T-Life; $5 payment support fee in stores and $10 through Customer Care (not modelled: the engine has no agent channel). Methods: Visa/Mastercard/Amex/Discover, bank account (ACH checking or savings), T-Mobile MONEY debit card, PayPal. AutoPay draws about two days before the due date by default (leadDays=2) and the withdrawal date can be moved to another day except the 29th-31st (days 1-28); the AutoPay discount needs a linked bank account (Pay by Bank), the T-Mobile Visa or a debit card on an eligible plan (other credit cards and wallets don't qualify). Cancelling the account does not cancel AutoPay. Payment Arrangements are self-service only (T-Life / My T-Mobile / automated line), for postpaid accounts less than 30 days past due; AutoPay pauses during an arrangement; $20 restore fee per line if suspended. Cancelling Home Internet requires contacting T-Mobile (no online cancel; the Home Internet contact page lists 1-844-275-9310, labelled tech support, and 1-844-839-5057 for sales — 1-844-275-9310 is used); the gateway must be returned within 45 days or a non-return fee up to $370 applies ($79 for excessive damage). Plan changes are done in a store or by contacting T-Mobile (capabilities.change_plan unsupported). Plan prices are not modelled. Paperless billing is managed in the T-Mobile account. The pay-your-bill page says to pay by phone through Customer Care without printing a number; contact.payPhone uses the Home Internet customer service number 1-844-275-9310 from the contact page.

help.title: Ways to pay your T-Mobile bill
paragraphs: Paying online or in the T-Life app has no fee. Log in to pay your own bill, or choose Pay as a guest to pay without logging in.
A $5 payment support fee applies to payments made in a store, and a $10 payment support fee applies to payments made through Customer Care.

Accepted: Visa, Mastercard, American Express and Discover (credit or debit), checking or savings (ACH), the T-Mobile MONEY debit card and PayPal; cash in stores only. Mailed checks go to T-Mobile, P.O. Box 742596, Cincinnati, OH 45274-2596; allow at least five days.

help.title: AutoPay
paragraphs: AutoPay is free and pays your bill automatically from a linked bank account, debit card or credit card. Payments come out about two days before the due date by default; you can choose another withdrawal date in T-Life or My T-Mobile, except the 29th, 30th or 31st. A bill due the day after you enroll may already be paid automatically.

To get the monthly AutoPay discount on an eligible plan you must be enrolled when the bill is made, have paid last month's bill on time, and pay with a linked bank account (Pay by Bank), the T-Mobile Visa or a debit card. Other credit cards and Apple Pay or Google Pay don't qualify, and paying early with an ineligible method removes the discount from the next bill.
Unprocessed AutoPay payments are retried after five banking days. Cancelling your account does not cancel AutoPay, so turn it off separately.

help.title: Payment Arrangements
paragraphs: Payment Arrangements are self-service only: set them up in T-Life or My T-Mobile. They're for postpaid accounts less than 30 days past due; anything 31 or more days past due must be paid first.

In T-Life, open the Account tab, choose Set up a payment arrangement, adjust the amount, method and date, then select Agree and Submit. AutoPay pauses while the arrangement is active and resumes after it's completed; a failed arrangement removes you from AutoPay.
Late fees may apply for dates after the original due date, and if the account is suspended a $20 restore fee per line (up to three lines) is added to the installments.
steps: Choose Set up a payment arrangement.

help.title: Cancel Home Internet
paragraphs: To cancel T-Mobile Home Internet, contact T-Mobile Home Internet customer service at 1-844-275-9310 (listed with 1-844-839-5057 for sales); it can't be done online. You need to return the gateway within 45 days or you'll be charged a non-return fee of up to $370. If the returned gateway has excessive damage, a one-time $79 charge is added within one or two bill cycles.

help.title: Your first Home Internet bill
paragraphs: Your first bill covers Home Internet from the day the gateway ships to the end of your first month, and is due within 21 days of shipping. Existing T-Mobile customers may also see the second month on the first bill, so it can look higher than usual.
To change your plan, visit a T-Mobile store or contact T-Mobile.

extra.intent: Using T-Mobile's help pages, find the payment support fee T-Mobile charges when a bill payment is made through Customer Care, and how to avoid it. Do not make a payment.

solution.text: Payments through Customer Care carry a $10 payment support fee; paying online or in T-Life is free.

extra.intent: A T-Mobile Home Internet customer is cancelling. Look up how many days they have to return the gateway before a non-return fee applies. Do not change anything on the account.

solution.text: The gateway must be returned within 45 days or a non-return fee of up to $370 applies.
